title: Development of a test in German language to assess middle school students’ physics proficiency
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the lack of readily accessible German-language, subject-specific achievement tests for middle-school physics. The authors aim to develop a test that can be used in educational research to assess students’ physics proficiency in a test-economic, objective manner, replacing ad hoc pencil-and-paper measures assembled from published TIMSS items.

The intervention/approach is not a teaching intervention, but a test-development process. The authors selected 40 physics-related TIMSS items, translated English items into German, and converted some open-ended items into multiple-choice single-select format. They then administered the resulting item pool to 177 eighth-grade students in Hamburg, Germany and used Rasch modeling to evaluate item fit, differential item functioning, reliability, and correlational validity with science interest, science self-concept, physics grades, and cultural/economic capital.

The final instrument retained 20 items spanning content areas typical of middle-school physics, especially mechanics and optics. The results suggested adequate model fit, sufficient person-separation reliability, excellent item-separation reliability, and expected correlations with external variables, leading the authors to conclude that the test provides a valid measure of middle-school students’ physics proficiency in German. They also note that the test is limited by its Hamburg-only sample and weaker coverage of electrics and the extreme ends of ability.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a correlational/test-development study using Rasch analysis, not an RCT or quasi-experiment. It provides useful psychometric evidence, but the design does not support causal claims about an educational intervention.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper has no direct instructional effect on achievement; its contribution is a validated assessment instrument. Any practical impact is indirect and modest, mainly improving measurement efficiency and research capability rather than student learning outcomes.

finding.finding_summary: The paper reports development and psychometric validation of a German-language middle-school physics proficiency test based on adapted TIMSS items, not an intervention effect. In a sample of n=177 eighth-grade students, the resulting 20-item test showed acceptable Rasch model fit (Andersen LR=11.82, df=19, p=0.89), person-separation reliability of 0.78, and item-separation reliability of 0.97, supporting valid measurement of physics proficiency.
finding.measure: Physics proficiency test scores / Rasch person parameters; item fit and reliability indices

finding.finding_summary: The test was explicitly designed to be highly test-economic and objective, using 20 multiple-choice single-select items with an estimated completion time of 20 minutes. This is a measurement-development finding rather than a student-outcome effect, but it indicates improved efficiency for assessing middle-school physics proficiency compared with longer open-ended formats.
finding.measure: Test length / estimated administration time / objective scoring properties
